item.title: Bottle Listing From One Photo

turns.text: This is my only product photo. Turn it into three separate square listing images: a clean white-background shot, a lifestyle shot on a gym bench, and a close-up of the lid and matte finish. Keep my exact black bottle, don't add branding or text.

item.tests: Tests turning one attached product photo into three finished listing images while preserving the source product's identity.

answer_sheet.Source product: Use the matte black insulated bottle in product-bottle.jpg as the reference for all three images.
answer_sheet.Required views: A clean white-background shot, a gym-bench lifestyle shot, and a close-up of the lid and matte finish.
answer_sheet.Product changes: Keep the original bottle's shape, proportions, lid design and matte black finish. Do not invent branding.
answer_sheet.Photography style: Realistic listing photography; lighting and gym styling are your call.
answer_sheet.Size and delivery: Three separate square images; 640 × 640 is fine.

must_haves: There are three separate square images, not a collage.
The bottle in every image matches the attached photo's silhouette, proportions, lid and matte black finish.
The white-background image shows the entire bottle with the original wooden table removed.
The lifestyle image places the bottle convincingly on a gym bench.
The close-up clearly shows the lid and matte surface without inventing new product features.
No added text or branding appears.

turns.text: This pic is my only product photo. Turn it into three separate square listing images: a clean white-background shot, a lifestyle shot on a gym bench, and a close-up of the lid and matte finish. Keep my exact black bottle, don't add branding or text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
I haven’t run anything or spent any credits.

### Lowest-cost AI option for all three
Use the free-plan **Flux 2 Klein** editor at **640 × 640**, generating each image separately.

| Image | Listed starting cost |
|---|---:|
| Clean white background | 5 credits |
| Gym-bench lifestyle scene | 5 credits |
| Lid and matte-finish close-up | 5 credits |
| **Expected total** | **15 credits** |

That’s based on the listed starting rate—not a verified checkout quote. I can’t check your current balance or confirm the final charge with the tools available here.

### Cheaper alternatives
- **About 10 credits:** generate only the white-background and gym-bench images; make the close-up by manually cropping your original photo in a free editor. This also preserves the actual lid and finish better than regenerating them.
- **No generation credits:** manually cut out the bottle onto white and crop the close-up. The gym-bench scene would require a separate background and manual compositing.

**640 × 640 is the smallest listed free-plan option.** Shorter doesn’t apply to still images; fewer generations is the useful saving here.

One important limitation: AI editing can subtly change the bottle’s shape, lid, or texture. I can explicitly request preservation of your black bottle with **no branding or text**, but can’t guarantee pixel-exact preservation. Manual cutout/cropping is safer when “exact” is essential.

Would you like to authorize the **three-image AI route at an expected 15 credits**, or use the **two-generation route at an expected 10 credits**, with a manual crop for the close-up?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that — the cheaper two-generation route at an expected 10 credits, with a manual crop for the close-up.

turns.agent:
The first edit was **refused for insufficient credits**. The tool reports that nothing was generated; no generation credits were spent. I stopped without attempting the second edit.

The expected 10-credit route can’t run with your current balance. No output files were created.

For the **free manual close-up**, open your original in a photo editor, select a square crop, and frame the carry loop, full lid, and upper shoulder so the matte finish remains visible. Export at the crop’s native size to avoid blurring. This preserves your actual bottle without AI changes.

You can also make the white-background image without generation credits using a free cutout tool. The gym-bench version would need manual compositing or sufficient Magic Hour credits.

One additional consideration: Magic Hour’s workflow guidance says commercial use requires a paid subscription, credit-pack purchase, or an agreed paid-usage arrangement—check its terms before using generated images in listings.
